problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062142/assets/cd21413d8eea5e2fec67eebe22967c846fd7916fd4fb0fbe5f8efe7ac9df6b1a.png)

The curve $C$ is given by $y=1-x$ from the point $(0,1)$ to the point $(1,0).$ Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=\,i+\,j$ through $C,$ measured with respect to the unit normal vector $n$ on $C,$ as shown above.
worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ measured with respect to a unit normal vector $n$ on $C$ is given by

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={\int }_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x.
$$

To apply this formula, 

- the curve should be parameterized as $r(t)$ for $t\in [a,b],$ and

- the unit normal vector $n$ *must* be a ${90}^{∘}$ clockwise rotation of the unit tangent vector $T(t).$

Parameterizing the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t,\,y=1-t,\,t\in [0,1].
$$

 

This parameterization traverses the curve from the point $(0,1)$ to the point $(1,0).$ Therefore, $n$ is indeed a ${90}^{∘}$ clockwise rotation of $T,$ so we can apply the above formula for the flux. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062142/assets/e288ed1095be61e4645fb63c22b7fd2cb605d34795c30557e84afb31b7ec8721.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & =1, \\ Q(x,y) & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-t)=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(1)\cdot (-1)-(1)\cdot (1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-2\,\text{d}t \\  & =(-2t){|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-2-0 \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12

The curve C is given by y=1−x from the point (0,1) to the point (1,0). Calculate the flux of the vector field F(x,y)=i+j through C, measured with respect to the unit normal vector n on C, as shown above.

a
−2
b
−1
c
1
d
0
e
2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

If F=Pi+Qj is a vector field and C is a piecewise-smooth, simple curve, then the flux of F across C measured with respect to a unit normal vector n on C is given by ∫CF⋅nds=∫CPdy−Qdx. To apply this formula,

  • the curve should be parameterized as r(t) for t∈[a,b], and

  • the unit normal vector n must be a 90∘ clockwise rotation of the unit tangent vector T(t).

Parameterizing the curve C, we have x=t,y=1−t,t∈[0,1].

This parameterization traverses the curve from the point (0,1) to the point (1,0). Therefore, n is indeed a 90∘ clockwise rotation of T, so we can apply the above formula for the flux.

Therefore,

P(x,y)=1,Q(x,y)=1.

Computing the derivatives of x(t) and y(t) along the curve, we get

dxdt=ddt(t)=1,dydt=ddt(1−t)=−1.

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

∫CF⋅nds=∫CPdy−Qdx=∫01(P⋅dydt−Q⋅dxdt)dt=∫01(1)⋅(−1)−(1)⋅(1)dt=∫01−2dt=(−2t)|01=−2−0=−2
